key_insight: The paper defines a continuous-tone analogue of simple points via a cyclic gradient and uses an ℓ0-norm formulation to detect topology-changing pixels in grayscale images, producing a topology-aware, differentiable-friendly criterion for training segmentation networks.
problem_solved: Existing simple-point detectors are binary and non-differentiable, preventing topology-preserving constraints from being directly used in gradient-based deep learning; this work provides a continuous, trainable measure to preserve topology during segmentation.
method: Define a cyclic gradient operator for continuous-tone (grayscale) images and characterize pixels that change topology via this operator.
Formulate an ℓ0-norm of the cyclic gradient to count topology-relevant points, and introduce a differentiable surrogate/relaxation suitable for backpropagation.
Integrate the topology-aware term as a loss component in data-driven segmentation models and validate improvements on topology-sensitive benchmarks (e.g., preserving connectivity, holes, skeletons).
impact: Enables end-to-end training of neural segmentation models that explicitly preserve topological features, improving structural plausibility in applications like medical imaging, remote sensing, and shape analysis.
visual_elements: Schematic of the cyclic gradient on a local patch showing how continuous-tone simple points are detected
Side-by-side segmentation results with vs. without the topology loss highlighting preserved/removed holes and connectivity
Flowchart showing loss composition: cross-entropy/IoU + ℓ0(cyclic gradient) surrogate → backprop into segmentation network
Bar or scatter chart comparing topology metrics (e.g., Betti numbers, connectivity errors) across methods
paper_title: Continuous-tone Simple Points: An $\ell_0$-Norm of Cyclic Gradient for Topology-Preserving Data-Driven Image Segmentation
paper_authors: Wenxiao Li, Faqiang Wang, Yuping Duan, Li Cui, Liqiang Zhang
